title: Pushing Images to Docker Hub ☁️
description: Authenticate, tag correctly, and push your own images to a registry for sharing.

slides.title: Registries & Repositories 🌐
slides.content:
# Where Do Images Live?

- **Docker Hub**: The default public registry (`hub.docker.com`).
- **Amazon ECR**, **Azure ACR**, **Google GCR/Artifact Registry**: Cloud provider registries.
- **Self‑hosted**: Docker Registry, Harbor, GitLab Container Registry, etc.

You **pull** images from them, and you **push** to share your own images.

slides.title: Creating a Docker Hub Account 🧑‍💻
slides.content:
# Free Account

1. Go to [hub.docker.com/signup](https://hub.docker.com/signup).
2. Choose a username (this is your **namespace**).
3. Verify email.

Once you have an account, you can create **repositories** (public or private).

slides.title: Logging In from the CLI 🔐
slides.content: Authenticate your local Docker client with Docker Hub:
slides.codeSnippet:
docker login
# Enter your username and password when prompted

# Or supply credentials non‑interactively (careful in scripts)
# docker login -u myuser -p mytoken

quizData.question: What does `docker login` do on your machine?

options.text: Authenticates you to a registry and stores credentials securely
Downloads the latest Docker image list

quizData.explanation: `docker login` saves your credentials in a local credential store, allowing you to push/pull private images.

slides.title: Tagging Before Pushing 🏷️
slides.content:
# The Push Formula

You can only push images to your own namespace. So an image must be tagged as:

`<your-dockerhub-username>/<repository>:<tag>`

**Workflow:**
1. Build or pull an image locally.
2. Tag it with your Docker Hub username.
3. Push.

```bash
docker tag alpine:3.18 myusername/alpine:3.18
docker push myusername/alpine:3.18
```

slides.title: Push Demo 🚀
slides.content: Let’s push a custom tag of Alpine to your Docker Hub (replace `myusername` with your real username):
slides.codeSnippet:
# Pull a base image
docker pull alpine:3.18

# Tag with your username
docker tag alpine:3.18 myusername/my-alpine:3.18

# Push
docker push myusername/my-alpine:3.18

# Output shows layers being pushed, then a digest

quizData.question: Why does `docker push nginx:latest` fail for most users?

options.text: Because nginx is not a valid image
Because you don't own the `library/nginx` namespace on Docker Hub
Because you need to be logged in

quizData.explanation: You can only push to repositories under your own Docker Hub username or organization. `nginx` belongs to the `library` namespace.

slides.title: Pulling from Your Own Registry 📥
slides.content:
# After pushing, anyone can pull (if public)

```bash
docker pull myusername/my-alpine:3.18
```

If you set the repository as **private** on Docker Hub, only authenticated users with permissions can pull.

To pull from a different registry, prefix the image name:
```bash
docker pull localhost:5000/my-image:latest
docker pull myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:1.0
```

slides.title: Authentication Beyond Login 🔐
slides.content:
## Personal Access Tokens

Docker Hub supports **access tokens** for CI/CD pipelines. Create one in your account settings, then:
```bash
docker login -u youruser -p your_token
```
Never expose your password in scripts.

slides.title: Beware of Pushing Sensitive Data 🛑
slides.content:
## Images Can Contain Secrets

If you baked a password or API key into an image layer, it will be visible to anyone who pulls that image. **Never** store secrets in images. Use environment variables, Docker secrets, or external vaults.
